<reason>A more convincingly defended the targeted proposition: assess full lifecycle costs, require benefits proportionate to implementation costs, and coordinate a supported transition. B raised a credible concern about fees being more flexible, but never established that meaningful phaseouts must be unsafe or require reusable substitutes. B also repeatedly misrepresented A’s inability to name a verified historical assessment as an admission that no assessments had ever occurred—even after A explicitly corrected that inference. A answered the pressure more honestly and supplied the cleaner comparative case.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A dismantled B’s “trivial or dangerous” dilemma: removing unnecessary packaging need only justify its own modest adjustment costs, while broader restrictions require stronger evidence. A’s closing also exposed that a fee producing the same phaseout would not eliminate the transition costs B emphasized.</best_rebuttal>
